speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this persistent, dry cough for about three months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but it does make me feel quite short of breath when I try to play basketball. However, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pneumonia (likely atypical or viral given the dry cough and ground-glass opacities). Given the three-month duration, we should also consider chronic interstitial lung disease or organizing pneumonia; do you have any history of autoimmune disorders or recent viral infections?
